question.text: Where will the great white shark Percy be on December 15, 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves as the closest landmass due west of the shark Percy according to the most recent ping at his [Ocearch tracker](https://www.ocearch.org/tracker/detail/percy) as of December 15, 2026.
question.fine_print: For example, the ping on July 6, 2026 had Florida being due west of Percy. Thus a question resolving then would have been the option corresponding with that location.

research:
I couldn't get Percy's current position. The OCEARCH tracker page loads through JavaScript, and my fetches returned only the page title with no ping data. The newest date I found is an August 11, 2026 ping, which a search summary attributed to the OCEARCH profile. I found no reports of any Percy ping in September, October or November 2026.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-08: Fetching the [OCEARCH Percy tracker](https://www.ocearch.org/tracker/detail/percy) and its filter endpoint gave back only the title "OCEARCH Shark Tracker". The Mapotic API also failed, with a 401 error. I could not read the live coordinates.
- 2026-08-11 / 08-16: A search summary of the OCEARCH profile says the latest ping was August 11, 2026 and the latest Z-ping (a weak signal that doesn't give a usable location) was August 16, 2026. I could not see where the August 11 ping was or confirm these dates myself. If they are right, Percy had been silent for about 12 weeks as of today. [OCEARCH](https://www.ocearch.org/tracker/detail/percy)
- Percy is a subadult male, about 9 ft 9 in and 432 lbs when tagged in Mahone Bay, Nova Scotia, on 2025-07-28. [Fox Weather](https://www.foxweather.com/earth-space/great-white-shark-percy-long-island-new-york-ocearch)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. If Percy doesn't ping again before December 15, the question resolves on the old August ping, so its location (which I don't know) matters a lot.
- How "due west" works off Long Island is ambiguous. Ocean Beach on Fire Island sits at about 40.65°N, and a point 14 miles south of it is roughly 40.45°N. At that latitude, a line due west hits Staten Island (New York) or the Raritan Bay / Monmouth County shore (New Jersey). Points off southern New England often have Massachusetts (Cape Cod) or Maine due west. Points off Nova Scotia or the Gulf of Maine can have Nova Scotia or Maine due west.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-08 back to mid-August: I found no Percy-specific news. The articles collected by the news API are about other sharks, or about the Percy Jackson TV show.
- 2026-08-02: The NY Post and syndicated copies reported Percy about 14 miles off Ocean Beach, Long Island. [dnyuz/NY Post](https://dnyuz.com/2026/08/02/great-white-shark-percy-pings-14-miles-from-long-island-coast/)
- 2026-07-28: Fox Weather says the Long Island ping came exactly one year after tagging, which was a Tuesday. Less than a day earlier he had been off Sea Isle City, New Jersey. He had covered 4,660 miles in total and was "probably heading farther north toward cooler waters". [Fox Weather](https://www.foxweather.com/earth-space/great-white-shark-percy-long-island-new-york-ocearch)
- 2026-07-06: The question's fine print says that day's ping had Florida due west.
- 2026-05-11: He pinged about 30 miles southeast of Pensacola Beach, after earlier Gulf pings on April 21 and April 26 and a weak Z-ping on May 6. [AOL](https://www.aol.com/news/pensacola-beach-had-great-white-151710950.html)
- 2026-03-03: His first ping near Myrtle Beach, South Carolina. [Yahoo](https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/three-great-white-sharks-tracked-155813651.html)
- 2025-11 (unverified): A search summary claimed Percy was near Virginia's Eastern Shore in November 2025. A follow-up search found no Percy-specific report, and WAVY's article blocked my fetch.

## 4. Base rates
- Percy pings rarely. I found pings in March, April, May, July and August 2026, often weeks apart. Long silences of a month or more seem common for him, so the August position may still be the latest one on December 15.
- The usual pattern for Nova Scotia-tagged juvenile and subadult white sharks is to be in Canada or New England in summer and early fall. They move south from October to December, often to Virginia, the Carolinas or the Southeast, and spend the winter in the Southeast or the Gulf. Percy's own record matches this: Nova Scotia in July 2025, apparently mid-Atlantic in November 2025 (unverified), South Carolina in March, the Gulf from April to May, then back north to New Jersey and New York in July. The OCEARCH-tagged shark Bella was off the Virginia Eastern Shore in December 2025. [iHeart](https://www.iheart.com/content/2025-12-04-700-pound-great-white-shark-spotted-in-rare-migration/)
- In practice this means a fresh December ping would probably put him off the coast south of New Jersey. A stale August ping would probably put him off New York, New Jersey or New England, depending on where the August 11 ping actually was.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no prediction market or expert forecast on Percy. None of the Kalshi markets that were collected are related to this question.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Any new ping between now and December 15 would replace the August position. Pings depend on the shark's dorsal fin breaking the surface, and seasonal migration south usually peaks from November to December.
- Media reports of Percy pinging, for example from Virginia or Carolina outlets, would be early signs of a new position.
- Recommendation: before you finalize, check the live OCEARCH tracker in a browser. You need the date and coordinates of the latest ping, and in particular the location of the August 11 ping.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. I found no reports of Percy pinging in September, October or early November 2026.
- **Key point:** the question resolves on the *most recent* ping as of Dec 15. Tagged sharks often go weeks or months without surfacing long enough to ping. If Percy stays silent, the answer is fixed by his last summer ping. That ping was probably off New York, or further north if he kept heading toward cooler water.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-03: Fox Weather reported the seasonal southward migration. Since late October, Ernest pinged off New Jersey (Nov 2), Penny in Florida's Gulf waters (Nov 2) and Nori off Rhode Island (Oct 31). Percy is not mentioned. [Fox Weather](https://www.foxweather.com/earth-space/great-white-sharks-seasonal-migration-south)

- 2026-08-01/02: On 2026-07-28, exactly a year after tagging, Percy pinged about 14 miles off Ocean Beach, Long Island (New York). In less than a day he had moved there from off Sea Isle City, New Jersey. He had covered about 4,660 miles in total, and the article suggests he was heading north toward cooler water. [Fox Weather](https://www.foxweather.com/earth-space/great-white-shark-percy-long-island-new-york-ocearch), [NY Post via dnyuz](https://dnyuz.com/2026/08/02/great-white-shark-percy-pings-14-miles-from-long-island-coast/)
- 2026-07-06: The question's fine print says Florida was due west of Percy on that date, meaning he was off Florida's Atlantic coast.
- 2026-05-11: Percy pinged about 30 miles off Pensacola Beach, his second ping there. He had travelled about 3,000 miles in nine months, and a report expected him to head back toward Nova Scotia. [AOL](https://www.aol.com/news/pensacola-beach-had-great-white-151710950.html), [The Advocate](https://www.theadvocate.com/baton_rouge/news/great-white-shark-florida-coast/article_4c07d630-ebbf-5cb3-a135-cb4dda22cf03.html), [WKRG](https://www.wkrg.com/northwest-florida/escambia-county/great-white-shark-tracked-near-coast-of-pensacola-beach/)

## 4. Base rates
- **His own pattern:** from 2025 to 2026 Percy went from Nova Scotia (July) to the Gulf of Mexico (by spring, Pensacola in May), then Florida's Atlantic coast (July 6), then New Jersey and New York (late July). So last winter he was well south of New Jersey.
- **General pattern:** young white sharks in the Northwest Atlantic usually leave New England and Atlantic Canada in October and November. They spend the winter from the Carolinas to Florida and the Gulf. By mid-December, sharks that ping are usually off the Carolinas, Georgia or Florida, or in the Gulf. Some stragglers ping off New Jersey or Virginia in early to mid-December. Early-November pings of other sharks off New Jersey and Rhode Island fit this timing. [Fox Weather](https://www.foxweather.com/earth-space/great-white-sharks-seasonal-migration-south)
- **Caution on "due west":** if Percy is in the Gulf (for example off the Florida Panhandle or Louisiana), the closest land due west could be Texas or Louisiana. Those still count as "south of New Jersey". Positions far offshore could still land in "south of New Jersey" if the line west hits the US coast. "Anywhere else" would mainly cover positions where the line west misses these listed areas, for example east of the Bahamas or in the Caribbean.
- **Ping gaps:** Percy seems to have pinged rarely. The press reports are months apart (May, July, then possibly mid-August), and I found nothing after mid-August, a gap of almost three months.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no prediction market or expert forecast on Percy's location. None of the Kalshi markets supplied are relevant (they cover College GameDay, recessions, bills and Dana White).

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- **Mid-November to mid-December:** peak southward migration. A new ping from Percy would most likely come from somewhere between New Jersey and Florida or the Gulf.
- **Possible news triggers:** OCEARCH social posts or local news stories about pings near the coast. These usually come out within 1 to 3 days of a ping.
- **Tag issues:** if the tag's battery is failing or it has stopped transmitting, the last summer ping (about Aug 11 to 16) would decide the question. Before forecasting, it is worth checking the live OCEARCH tracker by hand to get the date and location of the latest ping.

**(a) Time left:** about 37 days, until December 15, 2026. The answer depends on the latest OCEARCH ping as of that date.

**(b) Status quo:** The most recent reported ping is August 11, 2026 (unverified), and its location is unknown. The last confirmed location is August 2, about 14 miles off Ocean Beach, Long Island. A line due west from there plausibly hits New York (Staten Island or Rockaway) or the Sandy Hook / Monmouth shore in New Jersey. Fox Weather said he was "probably heading farther north," so the August 11 ping could instead be off Rhode Island or Massachusetts, or further north. If Percy stays silent, one of these northern answers wins.

**(c) Base rates:**
- Nova Scotia-tagged subadult white sharks usually migrate south between October and December, toward Virginia, the Carolinas or the Southeast.
- If Percy pings in late November or December, about 70-75% of such positions would be south of New Jersey.
- Percy pings infrequently, often with gaps of a month or more. He has already been silent about 12 weeks, so the chance of a fresh ping before December 15 is roughly 45%.
- Last autumn he reportedly pinged off Virginia's Eastern Shore in November 2025 (unverified), which supports the idea that he can ping during migration.

**(d) Strongest evidence:**
- July 28 and August 2, 2026: Percy pinged off Sea Isle City, NJ, then off Long Island, NY, and was described as heading north.
- August 11, 2026: last reported ping (location unknown). August 16: last Z-ping, which gives no usable location.
- No reported pings from September through November 8.
- His seasonal pattern is consistent: the Gulf and Southeast in spring, back north in summer.

**(e) Unexpected scenario:** The August 11 ping was south of Martha's Vineyard or near Block Island, so the line due west hits Rhode Island or Connecticut ("Anywhere else"). Alternatively, a December ping far offshore or near Bermuda has no clear landmass due west.

**How I combined these:**
- Stale-ping branch (55%): New York 25%, Massachusetts 25%, New Jersey 15%, Anywhere else 12%, Nova Scotia 8%, Maine 7%, south of New Jersey 8%.
- Fresh-ping branch (45%): south of New Jersey 72%, New Jersey 8%, New York 6%, Anywhere else 6%, Massachusetts 5%, Nova Scotia 2%, Maine 1%.

Starting from a pure migration base rate (mostly "south of New Jersey"), I moved substantially toward the northern options. That is because a silent shark means the stale August position resolves the question, and Percy's ping record makes that likely. I kept wide spread across options because I don't know the August 11 location.
